claim: Try the product with sample data that is searchable, hides a non-match, and can be reset.
where: Landing first action, /demo/, README, and desktop first-run screen
sandbox: Fresh browser context opens /demo/, searches a non-match, asserts the result has display:none, then resets to MAPLE-742.

claim: The browser demo uses a separate demo storage key and Start for real clears it.
sandbox: Fresh browser context searches the demo, observes only demo:local-data-finder:query, chooses Start for real, and asserts that key is absent.

claim: The desktop sample uses demo-index.json and demo-sample, keeps the normal index intact, and Start for real removes both demo artifacts.
where: Desktop first-run screen, /demo/, Privacy, README, and .factory/demo.md
sandbox: Temporary app-data directory contains a normal index plus demo artifacts; the test persists demo data, discards it, and checks the normal index remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

claim: The static site loads no advertising, tracking pixels, third-party fonts, or analytics SDKs.
sandbox: Fresh browser context records every request during a demo search and permits only the site origin.

claim: The sample demo works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: A dedicated fresh browser context visits and service-worker-caches /demo/, goes offline, reloads, and asserts the demo heading remains visible.

claim: Desktop search runs locally and works without a network client, LLM, or archive service endpoint.
where: Landing privacy section, desktop settings, Privacy, and README
sandbox: Compiled desktop-core source and runtime dependencies are checked for network clients and archive endpoints.

claim: The v0.1 desktop app is free to download; no unavailable purchase or license flow is presented.
sandbox: The scope decision and product copy are checked for the free-download statement, while shipped product code is checked for the absence of a checkout or payment integration.

claim: Searches Markdown, plain text, HTML, mbox, and text-based PDFs.
sandbox: Temporary fixtures for all five formats are parsed; HTML script text is excluded and each searchable body is asserted.

claim: Hidden folders and unsupported files are skipped.
sandbox: A temporary source contains a visible text file, a dotfile, and an unsupported CSV; only the visible supported file is indexed.

claim: Indexes only the sources you choose.
where: Landing first-screen fact, landing how-it-works section, README, and desktop empty state
sandbox: A temporary selected folder and a sibling folder contain different records. Scanning the selected folder must not return the sibling record.

claim: Each indexed source shows its record count, extraction time, and parser errors.
where: Landing privacy section and desktop source rail
sandbox: A source with one readable record and one oversized file is scanned; its status records count, time, and the parser limit error.

claim: Exports current search results as CSV.
sandbox: The public export path writes a CSV with its header, a quoted result row, and the expected row count.

claim: Opens the matched record instead of the selected source root.
where: Landing how-it-works section, desktop result action, and README
sandbox: A nested record is searched and its result open path is asserted to be the record itself.

claim: Every result includes one local record path and extraction time.
where: Landing proof strip, landing walkthrough, desktop result list, and README
sandbox: A Markdown record, a text record, and two mbox messages are searched together. Every result must have one non-empty path and extraction time; exported rows must preserve both fields.

claim: Opening a source uses your operating system.
sandbox: The desktop command is checked to use Tauri's native opener plugin rather than an internal viewer or web request.

claim: Mail attachments stay closed.
sandbox: A multipart mbox fixture includes base64 attachment text; only the message body is indexed.

claim: Removing a source does not delete the original.
where: Landing privacy section, Privacy, and README
sandbox: Removing a source clears index records while the original temporary file remains unchanged.

claim: Encrypts extracted text and paths at rest.
where: Landing privacy section, desktop settings, and README
sandbox: An encrypted index envelope is checked for absence of plaintext path/text and for correct-password-only recovery.

claim: The encrypted-index envelope uses ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a key derived by Argon2.
sandbox: A persisted fixture is checked for a 16-byte salt, 12-byte nonce, opaque ciphertext, correct recovery, and wrong-password rejection.

claim: The encryption password stays only for the current app session.
where: Landing privacy section, desktop settings, and README
sandbox: A fresh app state loaded from encrypted-index storage begins locked with no in-memory password.

claim: PDF extraction has a 25 MB input cap and a 12-second safety limit.
sandbox: An oversize temporary file is rejected and a timed worker returns the documented limit error.

claim: The normal index stays in the operating system's app-data folder and replaces its JSON file safely.
sandbox: A temporary app-data directory contains a prior index and an unfinished temporary write. Loading preserves the prior index; an atomic replacement then writes the new index.

claim: Finds the source record for at least 80% of a 50-query archive benchmark.
sandbox: Fifty source-grounded records are queried independently and at least forty correct first results are required.

claim: Published release assets include SHA256 checksums, and the installers compare them before completing.
sandbox: Temporary release assets produce SHA256SUMS/latest.json, and both installer scripts contain the hash comparison.

claim: The landing page chooses the matching macOS, Windows, or Linux release asset.
where: README Install section and landing download button
sandbox: A fixture release manifest is matched against macOS Intel, Apple-silicon, Windows, and Linux browser signals. Each selection must use the corresponding release asset.

claim: v0.1 desktop builds are unsigned and the landing page says how to open them.
sandbox: The landing warning and release workflow are checked together: the workflow has no macOS or Windows signing certificate configuration.

claim: The landing page includes a three-frame captioned desktop walkthrough.
sandbox: A fresh browser context opens the landing page and asserts three visible images with three captions.
